answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation a mesa that only rises through verified work: every completed job leaves a pigment receipt, a signed mark that builds a visible history. A fresh identity starts at the mesa's base with no pigment, so an attacker cloning accounts must redo months of real work per copy. Entry is further hardened by a ferrous gate: each new identity must pass a hardware-bound, energy-costly attestation that cannot be parallelized cheaply, so spawning thousands of fakes costs more than the rewards they could steal.
